=== Formation 301 (301–351) ===
==== Overview ====
This was the first articulated car of the Enoden, created in 1956 at Toyo Koki by converting cars 113 (2nd generation) and 114 (2nd generation), which had been in use since 1953, combining the bodies of Tokyo Municipal Tram type 150 cars 154 and 155 (2nd generation), built by Tanaka Sharyo in 1927 and inherited in 1953 from the Oji Electric Tramway (predecessor of today's Toden Arakawa Line) type 200, with the Kisha Seizo-made bogies of Toden Suginami Line cars 261 and 262 (formerly Seibu Tramway 41 and 42). The sides were given a form similar to the later formations, such as by relocating doors, but the front retained its tram-like bumper, and the narrow side windows peculiar to early steel cars strongly preserved the vestiges of the Oji Electric Tramway era; formation 306, too, uses a body descended from the same Oji Electric Tramway type 200, so its appearance is similar.

==== Body and running gear ====
The body modifications were concentrated on the gangway-converted articulation side. At one end of the body, the cab was removed and the articulation-side end made a flush (flat) end with a gangway; the passenger door was moved toward the body centre by the width of one side window, and one side window was provided at the car end, so the window/door arrangement changed from 1D11D1 to 1D10D2. In addition, whereas the underframe at this part had been of low-floor type, it was instead changed to a structure in which the articulation part was slightly raised by a slope from the centre of the passenger compartment, and the lower edge of the body was cut up; an end beam was fitted at that end, with a spherical centre plate and side bearers. The rest of the body basically remained as on the donor car.

The front of the body is a three-window layout with all windows of equal width, made drop windows in wooden frames for operating the trolley pole; the headlight is flush-mounted on the roof above the front, with a bumper at the lower front, round tail lights at the upper left and right, and a vertically elongated destination-board holder in the centre. On the sides, the passenger doors are 794 mm-wide single sliding doors sliding toward the car end; the door pocket windows are fixed windows in 596 mm-wide wooden frames, while the others are 634 mm-wide single-stage drop windows in wooden frames with protective bars outside; the window beside the cab is a 596 mm-wide door pocket window.

As on the donor car, the interior had a low-floor structure with the underframe and floor at the cab-side car end lower; the floor height there was 961 mm above rail level, 54 mm lower than the 1,015 mm of the passenger compartment, connected by a slope. The cab-side passenger door in the low-floor section and the articulation-side passenger door relocated to the high-floor section by the articulated-car conversion are of the same door height but differ in their mounting position (height). For seating, longitudinal benches 5,520 mm and 1,633 mm long are placed between the passenger doors and toward the gangway end respectively; the seating capacity is 68 per formation and the standing capacity 82. The cab has a driving desk at its centre and a length of 1,034 mm; between the cab and the passenger compartment there is only a simple partition at the centre.

On the roof, current-collecting trolley poles are placed at both ends of the formation, and small torpedo-type ventilators on the other parts. The couplers at both ends of the formation are the same small tight-lock automatic couplers as on the other formations, but at the time of introduction coupled operation was not carried out and they were only provisional.

The main controller is, like those of formations 302, 303, and 306 and the 500 series, a resistance-control type — a Toyo Electric Manufacturing ES-251A, motor-driven camshaft indirect automatic control with seven series and six parallel notches. As traction motors, it carries four Toshiba SE-118B DC series-wound commutator motors rated at 600 V and 42.3 kW — one on each of the front and rear bogies and two on the articulated bogie — but the cars added from formation 302 onward were changed to a configuration with two motors on each of the front and rear bogies and the articulated bogie made a trailer, and this arrangement has been inherited down to the present new 500 series. As a result, this car is an oddity in this respect. The drive has a gear ratio of 5.53, giving a rated tractive effort of 22.7 kN and a rated speed of 25.7 km/h. The braking system is electromagnetic SME braking (three-pipe straight air braking with an emergency pipe and solenoid valves), and two CP-27 motor-driven air compressors are carried.

The bogies are Kisha Seizo-made Baldwin-type with plate frames, from the donor cars; the intermediate bogie had its bolster modified for articulation, but otherwise the donor cars' bogies were basically used as they were. The bolster springs are leaf springs and the axle springs coil springs; the fixed wheelbase is 1,473 mm and the wheel diameter 838 mm; the traction motors are mounted outside the driving wheels by nose-suspended drive.

==== After entering service ====
Various modifications were also carried out after it entered service; formation 301, however, became a candidate for future scrapping from the second half of the 1980s and received no further improvement work, while having received relatively little attention when it was converted into formation 301, so its body and other modernization modifications were wide-ranging. The main ones follow those of formation 305; see the respective sections on that formation for details.
Change of current collector
When the changeover from trolley poles to Z pantographs was carried out from February 1964, formation 301 also removed its trolley poles and mounted one at the car end on the Fujisawa side. Later, during the changeover to (diamond) pantographs on all cars except the 100 series between February 1961 and May 14, 1973, formation 301 also carried one PT52 at the Kamakura-side car end for a while, after which the Fujisawa-side Z pantograph was also changed to a PT52. In the 1980s these were again changed to the PT4313-B-M.
Start of double-heading operation and change of couplers
With the start of double-heading using two articulated formations from June 21, 1971, the couplers at both ends of the formation were changed from simple tight-lock automatic couplers to top-suspended NCB-6 small tight-lock couplers, with the electrical coupler and coupling hose arranged alongside the coupler.
Others
In 1959 the bogies were modified at Tokyu Car Manufacturing: the bolster springs were changed from leaf springs to two Eligo springs and the bearings from plain (metal) bearings to roller bearings, and the bogie types became TS-408 (end bogie) and TS-409 (articulated bogie). In 1971 the bolster springs were modified again, from Eligo springs to a combination of two coil springs and one oil damper.
In the mid-1960s the destination display board was changed from a vertically elongated one to the slender, horizontally elongated one adopted on 500 series formation 502. At the same time, modifications were made such as changing the window sill from a moulding to a flat plate, changing the headlight from flush-mounted to an ordinary externally mounted shape, fitting window wipers, and changing the ventilators to Garland type.
Between 1971 and 1973, modifications were carried out on the 300 series to install crew compartment doors and passenger compartment partition walls, and formation 301 underwent these as well. In this formation, along with this the passenger door at the rear of the cab was moved slightly rearward and its opening direction changed from the cab side to the passenger compartment side, so the side window/door arrangement changed from 1D10D2 to dD9D2; the floor at the formation end, which had been of low-floor type, was raised, and the mounting height of the passenger door became the same as that toward the gangway end.
In the second half of the 1970s external loudspeakers were installed. Also, around 1979, at the same time as the repair of the runaway collision accident that occurred at Fujisawa Station, the headlight was moved from the upper front to the lower left and right and converted to two sealed-beam lamps, with the tail lights changed to square ones and mounted at the lower part; whereas on other formations of the 300 series these are mounted directly on the body, on formation 301 the headlight and tail lights are mounted via square pedestals. Around 1981 the side window frames were changed to aluminium sash and the door pocket windows to H-rubber mounting, and around 1987 the window headers were removed.
Formation 301 received no fundamental modernization, and in its final years was used as an advertising car for Meiji Seika, painted in a style reminiscent of the old “cooling trains” (nōryō densha). It was retired in 1992, replaced by 2000 series formation 2003. Of the bogies of formation 301, one that appears to be an articulated bogie is used as a temporary bogie at Gokurakuji Car Depot.

=== Formations 302 (302–352) and 303 (303–353) ===
==== Overview ====
In 1957, four cars of the 100 series (101–104) were made into two two-car articulated formations at Toyo Kōki; apart from the final years, these two formations had almost identical specifications. Cars 101 and 102 became formation 302, and cars 103 and 104 formation 303; on paper, cars 102 and 104 were reported as scrapped on April 2 of that year, so the registrations of 101 and 103 were inherited. Cars 101–104 were built in 1927 by Amemiya Seisakusho, four cars for 85,040 yen, entering the line in December of that year; they were the first bogie cars of the Enoshima Electric Railway, authorized for use on March 9, 1929, and entering service from April. At the time of conversion, their entrance steps had been raised in connection with the 1955 platform raising.

==== Body and running gear ====
As on formation 301, the body was modified based on the donor car's body: at one end the cab was removed and the articulation-side end made a flush end with a gangway, with an end beam fitted to the underframe below and a spherical centre plate and side bearers attached there. At the other end, the width of the central front window was enlarged and the lower bumper removed to make the lower edge of the body a straight line. On the sides, the passenger door was changed from a two-leaf sliding door sliding into the donor car's cab to a single-leaf sliding door sliding into the door pocket on the passenger compartment side, and the steps within the body were removed; the cab-side door was moved about 200 mm rearward to enlarge the cab space, and the articulation-side door was moved to a position 3,027 mm from the articulation-side car end. Meanwhile, the side windows, and the rivets and mouldings on the cornice and the side panels at the body centre, basically remained as on the donor car; the window headers were not fitted even on the donor car, and instead the cornice was formed as a plate lapped over the filler panel, which remained so after conversion; the window sills were also retained, but these were changed to a flat-plate form without rivets.

The front of the body is a three-window layout with a wide central window, each window being a drop window in a wooden frame for operating the trolley pole; the headlight is mounted on the roof above the front, with round tail lights of the same form as the donor car at the lower left and right of the front and a vertically elongated destination-board holder in the centre. The side window/door arrangement is 1D7D3; the passenger doors are 920 mm-wide single sliding doors; the door pocket windows are fixed windows in 760 mm-wide wooden frames, while the others are single-stage drop windows in wooden frames — those in the passenger compartment 605 mm wide with protective bars outside, and the one beside the cab 450 mm wide.

In the interior, longitudinal benches 5,040 mm and 2,647 mm long are placed between the passenger doors and toward the gangway end respectively; the seating capacity is 72 per formation and the standing capacity 78. The cab has a driving desk at its centre and a length of 1,218 mm; between the cab and the passenger compartment there is only a simple partition at the centre.

On the roof, current-collecting trolley poles are placed at both ends of the formation, and Garland-type ventilators on the other parts. The couplers at both ends of the formation are the same small tight-lock automatic couplers as on the other formations, but at the time of introduction coupled operation was not carried out and they were only provisional.

The main controller is the same resistance-control type as on formations 301 and 306 and the 500 series — a Toyo Electric Manufacturing ES-251A. As traction motors, it carries four Mitsubishi Electric MB-86B DC series-wound commutator motors rated at 600 V and 37.3 kW, two on each of the front and rear bogies; with a gear ratio of 3.88, the rated tractive effort is 20.9 kN and the rated speed 26.0 km/h. The braking system is electromagnetic SME braking (three-pipe straight air braking with an emergency pipe and solenoid valves), and two DH-16 motor-driven air compressors are carried.

The bogies were modified from the donor cars' Amemiya Seisakusho-made Baldwin-type plate-frame bogies; the intermediate trailer bogie was modified for articulation, and the bolster springs were changed from leaf springs to a combination of two coil springs and an oil damper, but, unlike formation 304 later, the bearings remained plain (metal) bearings. The fixed wheelbase is 1,375 mm and the wheel diameter 762 mm; the traction motors are mounted outside the driving wheels by nose-suspended drive.

==== After entering service ====
Various modifications were also carried out after they entered service; formation 302, however, became a candidate for future scrapping from the second half of the 1980s and received no further improvement work, and thereafter had an appearance different from formation 303. The main modifications follow those of formation 305; see the respective sections on that formation for details.
Change of current collector (formations 302 and 303)
When the changeover from trolley poles to Z pantographs was carried out from February 1964, formations 302 and 303 also mounted one at the Fujisawa-side car end, but on formation 302 the Kamakura-side trolley pole was retained for a while. Later, during the changeover to (diamond) pantographs on all cars except the 100 series between February 1961 and May 14, 1973, formation 302 also carried one PT52 at the Kamakura-side car end for a while, after which the Fujisawa-side Z pantograph was also changed to a PT52. In the 1980s these were again changed to the PT4313-B-M.
Start of double-heading operation and change of couplers (formations 302 and 303)
With the start of double-heading using two articulated formations from June 21, 1971, the couplers at both ends of the formations were changed from simple tight-lock automatic couplers to top-suspended NCB-6 small tight-lock couplers, with the electrical coupler and coupling hose arranged alongside the coupler.
Thereafter, the changeover to D90 tight-lock couplers, 96-core electrical couplers, automatic uncoupling devices, and bottom-receiving draft gear, for labour-saving in coupling work, was carried out by February 1994; but because formation 302 was scheduled for scrapping it was carried out only on car 302 at the Fujisawa end, car 352 being left unmodified. Also, formation 303, owing to differences in its main controller and braking system, could not be coupled with formations from the 1000 series onward until the main controller and braking system change described below was carried out, and double-heading remained as before between the 300 and 500 series.
Conversion of the drive to cardan shaft and change of bogies and traction motors (formation 303)
The work to update the bogies and traction motors, carried out from 1989 to 1992 on the formations of the 300 and 500 series then not slated for replacement, was carried out on formation 303 in 1992 as well. In this modification the traction motors were changed to the 50 kW-rated TDK8005-A and the drive to the KD110-A-M, likewise of the flexible-plate hollow-shaft parallel cardan drive type; the bogies were changed, as on formation 305 modified in 1989, to TS-837 for the motor bogies at both ends of the formation and TS-838 for the articulated/trailer bogies.
Installation of air-conditioning and body renewal (formation 303)
In the same year, 1992, as the above changes to the bogies, drive, and traction motors, air-conditioning equipment was installed and body renewal work carried out. As in the air-conditioning installation carried out on formations 304 and 305 of the 300 series, the CU77AE1 of the CU77 family, made by Mitsubishi Electric with a capacity of 24.4 kW, was used, with the air-conditioning unit and air-conditioning control box mounted on the roof and the starting control box under the floor.
With the installation of air-conditioning, the roof was changed from wood to a steel-sheeted raised roof, altering the appearance. The interior was also renewed, beginning with the installation of air ducts in the ceiling and the application of flooring material to the floor. At the same time, the passenger door at the formation end on the side was moved rearward to match formations 304 and 305, and one window was provided between it and the crew compartment door. Subsequently, in 1994, the side windows were changed from drop windows to two-stage windows with the upper pane dropping and the lower pane rising.
Change of the main controller and braking system (formation 303)
In 1999, the change of the main controller and braking system carried out on formation 305 the previous year was also applied to formations 303 and 304: the main controller was changed to the ACDF-M450-789A-M — the same as on formations 1501 and 1502 of the 1000 series and on the 2000, 10, and 20 series, made by Toyo Electric Manufacturing, of motor-driven camshaft control type — and the braking system to the HRD-1D made by Nabco (now Nabtesco), an electro-pneumatic command type used together with dynamic braking and employing the E-type relay valve. As on formations 304 and 305, the master controller was not converted to one-handle operation owing to space constraints but was replaced with a new two-handle unit.
Others (formations 302 and 303)
In the mid-1960s the destination display board was changed from a vertically elongated one to the slender, horizontally elongated one adopted on 500 series formation 502. Rain gutters were also fitted at the same time.
Between 1971 and 1973, modifications were carried out on the 300 series to install crew compartment doors and passenger compartment partition walls, and formations 302 and 303 underwent these as well. In the second half of the 1970s the side window frames were changed to aluminium sash, the door pocket windows to H-rubber mounting, and external loudspeakers installed; moreover, by about this time the body rivets that had remained in places even after conversion had disappeared.
On formation 302 around 1980 and on formation 303 in 1979, the headlight was moved from the upper front to the lower left and right and converted to two sealed-beam lamps, with the tail lights changed to square ones and mounted at the lower part; a CG145-A, a 3 kVA-output static inverter, was also installed as the auxiliary power supply.
The auxiliary power supply of formation 303 was later changed to the RG-4032-A-M of 10 kVA output, the same as on the 20 series, and by around 1994 the motor-driven air compressor was changed from the DH-16 to the HB-1200S adopted on 1000 series formation 1101 and later.
Formation 302, like formation 301, was excluded from the modernization work and, replaced by the introduction of the 10 series, ran with a farewell headmark from March 1 to March 31, 1997, and was scrapped the following year, 1998. In its final years its old-fashioned appearance and interior — preserved because it had not been modified — made it popular with railway enthusiasts. After scrapping it was taken to a campsite in Minamikoma District, Yamanashi Prefecture, and the whole formation is used under the name “Enoden Bungalow.”
Formation 303 had originally undergone extensive modification work, and with the air-conditioning the body's centre had begun to sag. Perhaps for that reason, from 2006 onward it entered revenue service less often, and in the second half of that year it hardly entered revenue service at all, being occasionally stabled outdoors at Gokurakuji Car Depot. It ended operation with a two-shot photography event with formation 305 held at Gokurakuji Car Depot on September 22, 2007, and was scrapped at the end of March 2008. After scrapping, some equipment such as the bogies was reused for the new-type new 500 series formation 502 by the same method as formation 304 described below. The reason it ceased to be used on the revenue line in its final period was that it suffered a serious incident in which a door opened while running, and it reached the expiry of its inspection before the cause was determined, as well as the fact that it had long been a candidate for replacement by a new car.
The front section of car 303 of formation 303 is preserved in the waiting room of Enoshima Station, which opened on March 31, 2009, and is displayed between 6:00 and 22:00.

=== Formation 304 (304–354) ===
==== Overview ====
In 1958, of the 100 series cars 106–110, cars 106 and 109 were converted into an articulated car at Toyoko Sharyo Setsubi; on paper, car 109 was reported as scrapped on April 15 of that year, when formation 304 entered service, so the registration of 106 was inherited. Cars 106–110 were five cars built in 1931 by Niigata Iron Works, with bodies similar to cars 101–104 and 105, built by different makers, but smaller in both body width and height; whereas formations 301, 302, and 303 modified the donor cars' bodies as they were, formation 304 reconstructed the body using the underframe and other parts. For bogies, the Brill 76E2 used on the 200 series was modified and used, and accordingly the 200 series' bogies were exchanged for the NDE-1, the Niigata Iron Works-made Baldwin-type plate-frame bogies of cars 106 and 109. These bogies were the ones with which cars 31 and 32 — 1922 Kisha Seizo-made wooden cars of the Seibu Tramway — were equipped when they became cars 111 and 112 of the Enoshima Electric Railway in 1934, and through various circumstances came to be used on the 200 series.

==== Body and running gear ====
The body was once dismantled, leaving the underframe, and reconstructed; the body width was widened from the donor car's 2,156 mm to 2,400 mm and the interior width from 1,956 mm to 2,190 mm, and, like formation 305, it features a structure in which the body overhangs the underframe. The body length was slightly extended from the donor car's 11,260 mm (excluding the end bumpers) to 11,437 mm; moreover, to make the bogie-centre distance the same as formations 302 and 303 at 8,700 mm, the underframe length from the car-end-side bogie centre to the formation-end car end was shortened from the donor car's 3,335 mm to 3,050 mm, and correspondingly the distance from the car-end-side bogie centre to the articulation-side car end was lengthened. The car ends, which had been low-floor underframes, were converted to a flat-floor type; the roof was changed from wood to a steel-sheeted raised roof, and the body height rose from the donor car's 2,275 mm (high-floor section) to 2,510 mm, while the side window height remained the same as the donor car at 760 mm, with window sills and headers fitted.

The front of the body is a three-window layout with a wide central window, each window being a drop window in a wooden frame for operating the trolley pole; the headlight is flush-mounted above the front windows, with square tail lights at the lower left and right of the front and a vertically elongated destination-board holder in the centre. The side window/door arrangement is d1D6D3; the passenger doors are 920 mm-wide single sliding doors; the door pocket windows are fixed windows in wooden frames 760 mm wide and 760 mm high, while the others are two-stage windows in wooden frames with the lower pane rising and the upper pane fixed, 605 mm wide and 760 mm high.

In the interior, longitudinal benches 4,300 mm and 2,266.5 mm long are placed between the passenger doors and toward the gangway end respectively; the seating capacity is 60 per formation and the standing capacity 90. The cab has a driving desk at its centre and a length of 915 mm; from this formation onward a crew compartment door was newly provided, but between the cab and the passenger compartment there is only a simple partition at the centre.

On the roof, current-collecting trolley poles are placed at both ends of the formation, and Garland-type ventilators on the other parts.

The couplers at both ends of the formation are the same small tight-lock automatic couplers as on the other formations, but from this formation onward, in preparation for double-heading of articulated cars to increase capacity, electrical coupler sockets and air hoses were fitted at the front; on formation 304, facing the lower front of the body, the air hose is on the left and the electrical coupler on the right — the reverse of formation 305 later.

The main controller is, like those of the previous formations, a resistance-control type made by Toyo Electric Manufacturing, but it was changed from the ES-251A of formations 302 and 303 and the 500 series to the ES-158B, motor-driven camshaft indirect automatic control with five series and four parallel notches. As traction motors, it carries four Toyo Electric TDK-31SP DC series-wound commutator motors rated at 600 V and 56 kW, two on each of the front and rear bogies; with a gear ratio of 3.37, the rated tractive effort is 19.2 kN and the rated speed 38.0 km/h — the highest rated output and rated speed in the 300 series. The braking system is electromagnetic SME braking (three-pipe straight air braking with an emergency pipe and solenoid valves), and two DH-16 motor-driven air compressors are carried.

The bogies, as mentioned above, were modified from the Brill-made 76E2 with cast-steel bogie frames; the intermediate trailer bogie was modified for articulation, and the bolster springs were changed from leaf springs to a combination of two coil springs and an oil damper, with the bearings changed from plain (metal) bearings to roller bearings. The fixed wheelbase is 1,475 mm and the wheel diameter 840 mm; the traction motors are mounted outside the driving wheels by nose-suspended drive.

==== After entering service ====
Various modifications were also carried out after it entered service; the main ones are as follows and follow those of formation 305; see the respective sections on that formation for details.
Change of current collector
When the changeover from trolley poles to Z pantographs was carried out from February 1964, formation 304 also removed the trolley poles at both ends of the formation and mounted one at the Fujisawa-side car end. Later, during the changeover to (diamond) pantographs on all cars except the 100 series between February 1961 and May 14, 1973, formation 304 also carried one PT52 at the Kamakura-side car end for a while, after which the Fujisawa-side Z pantograph was also changed to a PT52. In the 1980s these were again changed to the PT4313-B-M.
Start of double-heading operation and change of couplers
Formation 304, together with formation 305, had been equipped with electrical couplers and coupling hoses in anticipation of double-heading, but with the start of double-heading using two articulated formations from June 21, 1971, its couplers and the like were serviced anew along with formation 305, and its simple couplers were changed from tight-lock automatic couplers to top-suspended NCB-6 small tight-lock couplers, with the electrical coupler and coupling hose arranged alongside the coupler.
Thereafter, the changeover to D90 tight-lock couplers, 96-core electrical couplers, automatic uncoupling devices, and bottom-receiving draft gear, for labour-saving in coupling work, was carried out by February 1994. Owing to differences in the main controller and braking system, it could not be coupled with formations from the 1000 series onward until the main controller and braking system change described below was carried out, and double-heading remained as before between the 300 and 500 series.
Conversion of the drive to cardan shaft and change of bogies and traction motors
The work to update the bogies and traction motors, carried out from 1989 to 1992 on the formations of the 300 and 500 series then not slated for replacement, was carried out on formation 304 in 1991 as well. In this modification the traction motors were changed to the 50 kW-rated TDK8005-A and the drive to the KD110-A-M, likewise of the flexible-plate hollow-shaft parallel cardan drive type; the bogies were changed to TS-837 for the motor bogies at both ends of the formation and TS-838 for the articulated/trailer bogies.
Installation of air-conditioning and body renewal
In the same year, 1991, as the above changes to the bogies, drive, and traction motors, air-conditioning equipment was installed and body renewal work carried out. As in the air-conditioning installation carried out on formations 303 and 305 of the 300 series, the CU77AE1 of the CU77 family, made by Mitsubishi Electric with a capacity of 24.4 kW, was used, with the air-conditioning unit and air-conditioning control box mounted on the roof and the starting control box under the floor.
In addition, the interior was renewed, beginning with the installation of air ducts in the ceiling and the application of flooring material to the floor accompanying the air-conditioning.
Change of the main controller and braking system
In 1999, the change of the main controller and braking system carried out on formation 305 the previous year was also applied to formations 303 and 304: the main controller was changed to the ACDF-M450-789A-M — the same as on formations 1501 and 1502 of the 1000 series and on the 2000, 10, and 20 series, made by Toyo Electric Manufacturing, of motor-driven camshaft control type — and the braking system to the HRD-1D made by Nabco (now Nabtesco), an electro-pneumatic command type used together with dynamic braking and employing the E-type relay valve. As on formations 303 and 305, the master controller was not converted to one-handle operation owing to space constraints but was replaced with a new two-handle unit.
Others
In the mid-1960s the destination display board was changed from a vertically elongated one to the slender, horizontally elongated one adopted on 500 series formation 502. Rain gutters were also fitted at the same time, but initially only on car 304 at the Fujisawa end.
Between 1971 and 1973, modifications were carried out on the 300 series to install crew compartment doors and passenger compartment partition walls; on formation 304, which had had a crew door from the outset, a partition wall was installed on this occasion as well.
In 1980 the headlight was moved from the upper front to the lower left and right and converted to two sealed-beam lamps, with the tail lights moved to the lower part at the same time; a CG145-A, a 3 kVA-output static inverter, was also installed as the auxiliary power supply. At the time of modification the upper headlight was not removed although unlit, so the car appeared to have three lamps; the auxiliary power supply was changed in 2001 to the RG-4032-A-M of 10 kVA output, the same as on the 20 series. Also, around the same year, 1980, the window frames were changed to aluminium sash, the door pocket windows to H-rubber mounting, and external loudspeakers installed; around 1986, with body repairs, the window headers were removed leaving only window sills.
By around 1994 the motor-driven air compressor was changed from the DH-16 to the HB-1200S adopted on 1000 series formation 1101 and later.
Of the three old bogies generated when the drive was updated, the two motor bogies were de-motorized, painted yellow, and used as temporary bogies for inspection and repair within the car depot, while the remaining one intermediate bogie — a rare Brill-type bogie of US origin when traced back — was transferred to and preserved at the Western Railway Museum in California, USA, where it can be viewed.
From 2002 it was repainted in the brown-and-cream two-tone said to be its former livery, and was nicknamed the “Choco-den” (Chocolate Train).
Subsequently, damage to the underframe from aging and salt damage was discovered, and from around September 2004 it was laid up out of service; after repairs it returned to service at the end of February 2005, but was scrapped on September 30 of that year. From September 4 until scrapping it was returned from the Choco-den colour to the current Enoden colour for operation. Although there were requests from residents along the line for it to be transferred to them, only the front section was cut off and preserved at the Gokurakuji Works, the rest being dismantled and disposed of. Its bogies and other parts were reused for the newly built new 500 series formation 501, which replaced it.

=== Formation 306 (306–356) ===
==== Overview ====
In 1956, cars 112 and 202, whose bodies came from former Tokyo Municipal Tram type 150 and 170 cars, were converted into a coupled car as the 200 series, and this was then re-converted into an articulated car. While coupled cars had large capacity, they were inconvenient on the sharp curves of this line, with greater lateral displacement at the coupling, and so, based on the good results of the articulated cars from formation 301 onward, it was converted to an articulated car in 1968, with a purification ceremony held on December 5 and service beginning that same day.

The bodies were, like formation 301, inherited from the Oji Electric Tramway type 200; car 306 is a Tanaka Sharyo-made body later of Tokyo Municipal Tram type 150, the same type as cars 301 and 351, while car 356's is a Kawasaki Sharyo-made type 170 body. For bogies, as mentioned above, it uses the NDE-1 — the Niigata Iron Works-made Baldwin-type plate-frame bogies that cars 106 and 109 had been equipped with, exchanged when formation 304 was converted in 1958.

Like formation 301, whose body roots are almost the same, it retained a bumper at the front, but its form differs, for example with larger doors because of the different conversion period. Also, this was the only formation of this series in which the headlight was fitted as two lamps below the windows from the outset, and it kept its wooden roof; on the other hand it had a number of features seen only on this formation, such as being no-sill/no-header with a destination blind fitted and the front painted in the so-called “Kintaro's belly-band” style — but because changing the destination blind display during the short turnaround time at Fujisawa and Kamakura stations was inconvenient, the destination blind was removed and a destination-board holder newly fitted, and the “Kintaro” livery was also abolished. The bodies of cars 306 and 356 of formation 306 were originally both of the same Oji Electric Tramway type 200, but because the manufacturers differed, the two cars differed in window dimensions and roof height, so the roof at the articulation is stepped between the two cars.

==== Body and running gear ====
The body modification followed that of formation 301, focusing on the gangway-converted articulation side. At one end of the body, the cab was removed and the articulation-side end made a flush end with a gangway; the passenger door was moved toward the body centre by the width of one side window and one side window provided at the car end, with the door's opening direction changed from the cab side to the passenger compartment side; and the door and door pocket were widened using the space of one passenger-compartment window. The underframe at this part, which had been of low-floor type, was changed to a flat structure, with an end beam fitted at the end and a spherical centre plate and side bearers attached. On the cab side too, the low floor was raised, the passenger door's opening direction changed from the cab side to the passenger compartment side, the door and door pocket widened using the space of one passenger-compartment window, and the window beside the cab changed to a narrow drop window. As a result of these modifications, the side window/door arrangement changed from the 200 series' 1D11D1 to 1D8D2, and the body's window sills, window headers, and rivets were removed, giving smooth body sides and front.

The front of the body is a three-window layout in wooden frames with all windows of equal width — the centre a fixed window and the left and right two-stage windows with the lower pane rising; at the lower front is a bumper, above it at the left and right round sealed-beam headlights and square tail lights, and above the central window a manually operated vertically elongated destination blind. On car 356, whose cornice is narrower, this window is slightly lower. On the sides, the passenger doors are single sliding doors widened from the 200 series' 790 mm to 1,100 mm; the door pocket windows are fixed and the others are two-stage windows in wooden frames with the lower pane rising — a modification made when the cars were transferred from Tokyo Municipal Tram to Enoshima Kamakura Kanko, differing from formation 301, which retained drop windows.

In the interior, longitudinal benches are placed between the passenger doors and toward the gangway end; the seating capacity is 64 per formation and the standing capacity 88. The cab has a driving desk at its centre, and between the cab and the passenger compartment there is only a simple partition at the centre.

On the roof, only a Z pantograph for current collection is fitted at the formation end of car 306 on the Fujisawa side; no ventilators are provided. The couplers at both ends of the formation are the small tight-lock automatic couplers carried over from the 200 series days, but at the time of introduction coupled operation was not carried out and they were only provisional.

The main controller is the same resistance-control type as on formations 301, 302, and 303 and the 500 series — a Toyo Electric Manufacturing ES-251A. As traction motors, it carries four Toyo Electric TDK-516C DC series-wound commutator motors rated at 600 V and 37.3 kW, two on each of the front and rear bogies; with a gear ratio of 3.42, the rated tractive effort is 11.6 kN and the rated speed 27.0 km/h. The braking system is electromagnetic SME braking (three-pipe straight air braking with an emergency pipe and solenoid valves), and two CP-27 motor-driven air compressors are carried.

The bogies were modified from the donor cars' Niigata Iron Works-made Baldwin-type plate-frame bogies; the intermediate trailer bogie was modified for articulation, and only this articulated bogie had its bolster springs changed from leaf springs to a combination of two coil springs and an oil damper, while the bearings, including those of the end bogies, remained plain (metal) bearings. The fixed wheelbase is 1,375 mm and the wheel diameter 762 mm; the traction motors are mounted outside the driving wheels by nose-suspended drive.

==== After entering service ====
Several modifications were carried out after it entered service; but because formation 306's conversion was in 1968, later than the other formations, and from the second half of the 1980s it became a candidate for future scrapping and received no further improvement work, it had fewer modification items than the other formations. The main ones follow those of formation 305; see the respective sections on that formation for details.
Change of current collector
During the changeover to (diamond) pantographs on all cars except the 100 series between February 1961 and May 14, 1973, formation 306 also carried one PT52 at the Kamakura-side car end for a while, after which the Fujisawa-side Z pantograph was also changed to a PT52. In the 1980s these were again changed to the PT4313-B-M.
Start of double-heading operation and change of couplers
With the start of double-heading using two articulated formations from June 21, 1971, its simple couplers were changed from tight-lock automatic couplers to top-suspended NCB-6 small tight-lock couplers, with the electrical coupler and coupling hose arranged alongside the coupler.
Others
Between 1971 and 1973, modifications were carried out on the 300 series to install crew compartment doors and passenger compartment partition walls, and formation 306 underwent these as well. At the same time the destination blind at the top of the front was removed and changed to the same slender, horizontally elongated destination display board as the other formations, and the central window on the front of car 356 was modified to the same height as the left and right windows. In the second half of the 1970s external loudspeakers were installed, and in the 1980s the side window frames were changed to aluminium sash, the door pocket windows to H-rubber mounting, and external loudspeakers installed.
It was scrapped in 1991 — the earliest of this series — being replaced by 2000 series formation 2002. Deterioration of the body from repeated modifications is thought to have been one cause.
章节.Additional notes:
For a long time it did not carry an automatic announcement device, but even then, when in four-car operation a car of another type equipped with an automatic announcement device was coupled behind in the direction of travel, automatic announcements were played. Conversely, even on cars equipped with automatic announcements, when the car behind was of this type, only voice announcements by the conductor were possible — a situation that continued until formation 305 was fitted in 2008 with an automatic announcement device with English announcements like the new 500 series. This also completed the installation of automatic announcement devices on all formations of the Enoden.

In the past it was often used as an all-over advertising car like the other types. It is particularly notable that the entire body was painted gold as advertising livery for Sun Oil. As of 2008, the surviving formation 305 is in the conventional standard livery of pale green and cream.

Formation 303 appeared in a 2002 television commercial for Mitsubishi Electric's D504i mobile phone.

Initially one number was assigned to the two bodies, but following a 1960 notice from the Ministry of Transport, from formation 305 onward one number per body was adopted, as 305 and 355, and the existing formations 301–304 were also renumbered to one number per body.
章节.Operation: As of 2024, formation 305 is the only one still registered. Its operation is common with the other types, and when running as a four-car formation it is coupled with cars of other types.
